question: is the lag's ICC really zero, and can the within-fetus noise be fixed?
RETRACTION: I reported ICC = 0.000 and concluded the lag has no stable per-fetus value, unfixable by averaging or weighting. THAT WAS WRONG. Split-half reliability -- which makes no ANOVA assumptions -- is clearly non-zero and rises with the number of images.

test2_split_half.design: mean of a fetus's even-numbered images vs mean of its odd-numbered images; Spearman-Brown corrects half-length to full-length
test2_split_half.reading: reliability is real and increases with k exactly as measurement theory predicts: 0.12 at k>=2, 0.41 at k>=4, 0.53 at k>=6. A quantity with zero reliability cannot do this.

test1_heteroscedasticity.verdict: NOT the explanation. Dropping the high-variance early slots, or variance-standardising per slot, leaves ICC at exactly 0.0000 in every variant.

THE_REAL_CAUSE.reading: 40% of fetuses (353 of 883) have exactly ONE image. They carry zero within-fetus information but still enter MSB, diluting the between-fetus mean square while contributing nothing to MSW. Restricting to fetuses that actually have repeated measures gives ICC 0.027 -> 0.043 -> 0.062 -> 0.076 as the minimum image count rises. The positive control on the same unbalanced design recovers planted 0.30 and 0.10 correctly, so the estimator is fine -- the POPULATION was wrong.
THE_REAL_CAUSE.SUPERSEDED: see CORRECTION_to_THE_REAL_CAUSE -- the dilution mechanism is not supported

CORRECTED_ANSWER: The lag DOES have a stable per-fetus component; it is just small and heavily measurement-limited. Single-image ICC is roughly 0.03-0.08, but the reliability of a fetus's MEAN rises with k: ~0.41 at four images, ~0.53 at six. This resolves the tension I flagged -- a per-fetus mean with reliability 0.3-0.5 CAN correlate with birth centile at rho=+0.21, whereas one with reliability 0 could not.
SO_WHAT_CAN_BE_DONE: PRECISION WEIGHTING IS BACK ON THE TABLE. With ICC>0 and k varying 1-12, weighting each fetus by its own reliability (or a Kalman with per-visit variance sigma^2/k) is now well-motivated, not futile.
RESTRICT OR WEIGHT BY COVERAGE. The 223 fetuses with >=5 images have roughly 3x the reliability of the median fetus. An analysis on them trades n for measurement quality.
DISATTENUATION. Observed correlations are capped at sqrt(reliability); at ~0.41 the ceiling is 0.64, so the measured latent->lag R2 of 0.033 is an underestimate of the true association.
PER-PLANE CLOCKS (still untested) remain the route to raise single-image reliability at source.
caveats: ICC 0.03-0.08 is still small in absolute terms -- this rescues the lag from 'pure noise' to 'weak and measurement-limited', not to 'strong'
the >=k subsets are progressively selected populations; fetuses with many images may differ systematically (more scans often means more clinical concern)
split-half by slot parity could confound with acquisition order; the random-half version (0.274) is the more conservative estimate and is the one I would quote

CORRECTION_to_THE_REAL_CAUSE.what_I_claimed: ICC=0 is an artefact of 353 single-image fetuses diluting MSB; 'the estimator was fine, the population was wrong'
CORRECTION_to_THE_REAL_CAUSE.why_that_was_unsupported: my only control simulated the >=4-image subset, which contains NO singletons, so it could not test the mechanism it was cited for. A proper control on the FULL k-distribution (singletons included) recovers planted ICC 0.30->0.280, 0.10->0.080, 0.05->0.043 -- the estimator handles singletons correctly. Dilution is NOT the explanation.

what_the_data_actually_show.reading: single-image fetuses are a STRUCTURALLY DIFFERENT population, not a diluting one. Their lag variance is 0.98 against 6.54 for repeated-measure fetuses (0.15x), their mean is +0.74 against -0.11, and NONE of them sit in slot 0 -- the noisiest slot. Pooling two populations with a 6.7x variance difference and different means violates the one-way ANOVA's homogeneity assumption outright. The ICC=0 is a MIXTURE artefact, not a dilution artefact.

CORRECTION_to_THE_REAL_CAUSE.corrected_status: the numbers stand: ICC=0.000 pooled, 0.027-0.076 restricted, split-half 0.27-0.53. The CAUSAL ATTRIBUTION is corrected -- the pooled ANOVA is invalid because it mixes two populations with very different variances, not because singletons dilute MSB. The practical conclusion is unchanged: use the restricted/split-half estimates, which agree with each other.
